quick: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening
summary: Tafluprost is a topical (ophthalmic) prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue used to lower elevated intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. Instilled once daily in the evening, it reduces intraocular pressure mainly by increasing uveoscleral aqueous outflow. It is available as preservative-free single-dose drops (Zioptan) and is generally well tolerated; characteristic effects include conjunctival hyperaemia, gradual darkening of the iris, eyelid skin and eyelashes, and lash growth.
indications: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma
Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in ocular hypertension

dosage.d: One drop of 0.0015% solution in the conjunctival sac of the affected eye(s) once daily
If used with other eye drops, separate instillation by at least 5 minutes
dosage.n: Tafluprost given last if multiple drops

admin: Instill in the evening; more frequent dosing reduces the IOP-lowering effect
Wash hands; avoid touching the eye or surrounding structures with the dropper tip
Remove contact lenses before instillation and reinsert after at least 15 minutes
After instilling, close the eye and apply gentle nasolacrimal occlusion to reduce systemic absorption
If using more than one ophthalmic product, wait at least 5 minutes between them
moa: Tafluprost is a fluorinated analogue of prostaglandin F2-alpha that acts as a potent, selective agonist at the prostaglandin FP receptor. It lowers intraocular pressure principally by increasing uveoscleral (and to some extent trabecular) outflow of aqueous humour.

relative: Aphakia, pseudophakia with torn posterior lens capsule, or risk factors for macular oedema
monitor: Iris, periorbital and eyelash pigmentation/length changes
Signs of macular oedema in at-risk eyes

preg: Tafluprost should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary; prostaglandin analogues may have pharmacological effects on the uterus and there are insufficient human data, so it is not recommended.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is not recommended; it is unknown whether tafluprost or its metabolites pass into human milk, and animal data show excretion into milk.
renal: No dose adjustment is required; systemic exposure after ocular use is very low.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required; systemic exposure after ocular use is very low.

moderate: Other ophthalmic prostaglandin analogues - paradoxical IOP rise reported with combinations; avoid co-use
minor: Other eye drops - separate instillation to avoid washout
interactions.diagnostics: No relevant effect on systemic laboratory tests.

serious: Macular/cystoid macular oedema (especially in aphakic/pseudophakic eyes)
Periorbital fat atrophy / deepening of the lid sulcus
emergency: Sudden vision loss or marked eye pain (seek urgent ophthalmic care)

monitoring: Intraocular pressure to confirm therapeutic response
Iris, eyelid and eyelash pigmentation and lash length (often irreversible iris change)
counsel: Use one drop in the evening each day - using more often works less well
Your iris may slowly turn more brown, and your eyelashes may grow longer/darker; iris change can be permanent
Eyelid skin may darken (usually reversible) - applying carefully and wiping away excess helps
Remove contact lenses before use and wait 15 minutes before reinserting
Report eye pain, marked redness or vision changes promptly
pk: IOP reduction begins within ~2-4 hours of the first dose
Maximum IOP effect about 12 hours after instillation
Rapidly hydrolysed; tafluprost acid plasma half-life is short (systemic levels very low)
IOP-lowering effect maintained over 24 hours with once-daily use
Store unopened single-dose units refrigerated; once the pouch is opened, store at room temperature and use within the labelled period
pearls: Available as a preservative-free single-dose formulation (Zioptan), useful in ocular surface disease or preservative sensitivity
Dose once daily in the evening - more frequent use diminishes the IOP effect
Counsel patients about iris darkening (may be permanent) and eyelash/eyelid skin changes before starting
Caution and monitor for macular oedema in aphakic or pseudophakic eyes with a torn posterior capsule
Effective monotherapy; avoid combining with another prostaglandin analogue
missed: If a dose is missed, skip it and instill the next dose at the usual evening time; do not use a double dose to make up for the missed one.
overdose: Topical ocular overdose is unlikely to cause systemic effects because of low absorption; if excess drops are instilled, no specific treatment is needed beyond observation. Accidental ingestion is managed supportively.
